brief: Ten-year Treasuries had their worst session since April 2025's Liberation Day and 5-year yields topped 5% for the first time since 2007, even as Brent is up around 73% in 2026 and US CPI has risen from 2.4% in January to an expected 3.60% in September. DB argues this is not an inflation story: of the roughly 97bps rise in 10-year nominal yields this year, only around 10bps comes from breakevens, which have been stable for three-plus years; the remainder is real yields, now at 2008 levels. Term premium has stayed range-bound for 18 months, so fiscal fears aren't the driver either. The move is therefore about policy rates and a higher neutral rate. Warsh attributes higher yields to economic strength, competition for capital (which DB reads as AI capex), and geopolitical factors; Raskin argued 10 days ago the neutral rate, while elevated, sat within a plausible range toward its higher end, and DB now sees yields edging close to that upper bound. Yesterday's strong PMIs, Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 5.08% for Q3, and roughly 30% Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth added fuel, with positioning possibly amplifying the move.
